title: Telemetry Orchestrator: schema-aware, per-tenant metric transforms and backpressure control
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an orchestrator service that sits between Prometheus/OTel collectors and our KPI pipeline to provide schema negotiation, per-tenant metric transforms, lightweight edge sampling, and backpressure-aware buffering. Goals: (1) ensure stable, low-latency KPI delivery for inference hosts while bounding cardinality introduced by customer labels; (2) preserve Prometheus scrape compatibility and OTLP semantics; (3) allow runtime transform rules per-tenant (rename/aggregate/blacklist) and versioned metric schemas for downstream consumers. The orchestrator should support dagger-like pipeline stages: receiver adapters (prometheus/otlp), schema-translation, transform engine (rules DSL), sampler/sharder, envelope encoder, and adaptive backpressure buffer with tenant quotas.
tasks: Design schema negotiation protocol and versioning strategy (options: JSON schema + compatibility rules vs protobuf descriptors)
Prototype transform rules DSL and operator set (rename, map_labels, rollup, drop, hash-truncate)
Implement Prometheus remote_write adapter that emits OTLP-compatible envelopes
Build per-tenant policy store (config + staged rollout) with audit logs
Implement adaptive buffering/backpressure with tenant QoS and shed heuristics
Add cardinality bounding hooks and exemplar/tag-censoring rules
End-to-end performance tests and SLO verification (p95 < 200ms ingest latency under steady state)
Create migration/rollout plan and feature flag for gradual enablement
acceptance_criteria: Receiver accepts both Prometheus remote_write and OTLP metrics and maps to a common envelope format
Per-tenant transform rules can be applied without dropping non-target tenants' data
System enforces cardinality caps and emits enforcement counters to telemetry
Backpressure logic prevents OOMs and maintains 99th percentile ingest latency below 500ms at target load
Integration tests cover schema evolution: add/remove label, rename metric, and rollup semantics
Runbook updated and on-call playbook validated with chaos test that simulates downstream outages
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and console teams. Agreed to reuse existing policy store patterns from rollout-service.

2026-02-28: Spike: implemented a minimal prometheus->envelope adapter (prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/4128). Observed 2x CPU vs raw prom-receive due to label processing; need optimized label maps.

2026-03-05: Decision to use a compact envelope (msgpack + gzip) for internal bus to reduce network cost. Documented trade-offs in design doc (https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/telemetry-orchestrator-design).
2026-03-10: Implemented transform DSL v0.1 and unit tests. DSL supports rename, drop, label-map, and simple rollup. PR opened for review (https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/4163).
2026-03-12: Load test simulating 10k hosts shows burst buffer holds but p99 latency spikes during synthetic cardinality storm. Working on sharder + eviction policy.
decisions: Use OTLP envelope internally to unify Prometheus and OTLP metric semantics
Transform rules will be versioned per-tenant and include a safe 'dry-run' mode that emits diffs to an audit topic
Cardinality bounding will be implemented as a pluggable stage with both label-hash truncation and metric drop thresholds
Backpressure model: reactive shedding at receiver boundary with token-bucket per-tenant + exponential backoff signals to upstream collectors
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Excessive CPU for label-heavy metrics -> Mitigation: switch to interned label keys and precompiled regex transforms
Risk: Incorrect transform rules causing silent metric loss -> Mitigation: dry-run mode + automated schema-compat checks + alerting on dropped metric count
Risk: Tenant isolation breaches when applying transforms -> Mitigation: strict policy validation, per-tenant audit logs, and enforced RBAC on policy store
Risk: High cardinality attack vectors -> Mitigation: default deny high-cardinality labels, per-tenant quotas, and anomaly detectors that auto-shed
qa_steps: Deploy on a staging cluster with synthetic Prometheus scrapes (scale to 50k series)
Enable per-tenant transform in dry-run and validate emitted diffs for 3 tenants
Run chaos test simulating downstream Kafka outage and ensure backpressure and replay work
Verify that enforcement metrics surface in Console and generate alerts
